head: pr17399-r3
report:
The patch has one defect that must be fixed before merge, which I reproduced. I also found one smaller cleanup issue. The rest of the patch I only read partly in the 20 minutes; see the coverage note at the end. ## 1. A held request keeps its cross-process in-flight permit for the whole pause, which blocks other unpaused omp processes **Mechanism.** In `packages/ai/src/stream.ts`, `withProviderInFlightLimit` now takes the provider in-flight slot first (`acquireProviderInFlightSlot`, line 692). Only after that does it run the caller's hold (`holdBeforeDispatch(hold, options?.signal)`, line 701). The comment says this order is on purpose: "Last, so the slot wait above cannot outlast it". That slot is not limited to one process. It is a lease file under `getProviderInFlightRoot()` that records the pid and is kept alive by a 5 s heartbeat (`PROVIDER_INFLIGHT_HEARTBEAT_MS`). Every omp process configured with `maxConcurrency` / `maxInFlightRequests` for that provider shares these leases. So a request that reaches the chokepoint while `/pause` is engaged: 1. takes the lease; 2. waits on the closed gate for as long as the human leaves the pause on; 3. keeps sending heartbeats the whole time, so stale-lease cleanup never reclaims it. The patch also makes this much more likely than before. It adds `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(...)` to requests that start on their own while the session is paused: - cache-warmer refreshes (`cache-warmer.ts`, timer-driven); - sharpshooter consolidate and extract (timer-driven); - side-stream titles and compaction (`agent-session.ts` `#sideStreamFn`); - the agent-loop hold itself (`agent-loop.ts`), when the pause lands during preparation. Before this change, those requests either finished or were stopped by the loop's gate poll, which runs before any slot is taken. Now they park while holding the provider's concurrency budget. With `providers.

.maxConcurrency: 1`, pausing one terminal stops every other omp session using that provider until the pause ends. **Trigger.** Configure `maxConcurrency: 1` for a provider. Session A runs `/pause`, and its cache warmer or any side request fires. Session B, not paused, sends a prompt to the same provider. B waits until A resumes. **Measured.** Probe: `scratch/slot.test.ts`, run from `packages/ai`. Request A uses `maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }` and a `beforeDispatch` that never resolves, standing in for the closed gate. Request B uses the same limiter and has no hold. ``` lease entries while paused: [ "WYMOv…", "WYMOv…/953503-1793364825263-…", "…/info.json" ] unpaused request after 1501 ms: starved ``` B finished only after A's hold was released. **Fix direction.** Run the hold before acquiring the slot, then run it again after the slot is acquired, so the "slot wait outlasted the hold" case is still covered. Alternatively, release the lease while parked and take it again after the hold opens. ## 2. `wrapTransport` / the "live build" machinery has no production caller **Mechanism.** `StreamOptions.wrapTransport`, the `TransportWrapper` type, the `live` flag in the stamp, `layerWrapper`, and the code that pushes extra holds into a live build's shared `holds` array are all new in this patch. A search for `wrapTransport` across `packages/` (tests excluded) finds it only in `types.ts` and `transport-fetch.ts`; nothing in `agent` or `coding-agent` sets it. This adds the hardest-to-follow part of `transportFetch` without any user of it: - a stamped live build's `holds` array is changed in place, so a hold added through one reference gates every other reference to that fetch; - `withoutDispatchHold` gets a special case for it. **Trigger.** `grep -rn wrapTransport packages/*/src`: no consumer. **Fix direction.** Remove it from this PR and add it alongside the caller that needs it. If it stays, it needs a caller that shows the in-place `holds` mutation is safe across requests. ## Not covered or lower confidence (not confirmed as defects) - **Agent-loop watchdog.** The outer stream in `withProviderInFlightLimit` never calls `forwardLocalWorkFrom(inner)`. Now that every agent-loop request has a hold, every request goes through that outer stream, so the new `outer.forwardLocalWorkFrom(inner)` in `empty-completion-retry.ts` sees the chokepoint stream, not the provider stream. I did not find a watchdog that reads that layer, so I couldn't show a user-visible failure. - **Pre-response timer.** In `armPreResponseTimeout`, `suspend()` runs at transport entry. If a hold throws something other than an abort (`codexPrewarmHold`, `assertEphemeralTurnReady`), the guard stays suspended and its held-work window stays open until `clear()`. Every caller I checked clears in a `finally`, so this looks harmless. - I did not review the TUI changes (`packages/tui`: `keys.ts`, `native/backend.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `tui.ts`, `pause-screen.ts`) or the provider-specific transports (Codex websocket, Cursor, GitLab Duo).
